title: Switching a long recording to Edit never freezes the app, and its tool bar arrives with the slide
goal: Switching a long captioned recording from View to Edit slides smoothly, but the tool bar and the track rows fill in up to about 0.7s after the key, and now and then the app freezes for longer than 100 ms in that time (118.6 ms in the 2026-10-20 full sweep), which fails its walk. The panel may arrive just after the slide (settled on 2026-10-20, when the waiting cards were taken as recommended); the tool bar and track rows should arrive with it, and nothing should hold the app for 100 ms.
notes: Follows the-slide-into-edit-mode-draws-every-frame-like, which moved every stage after the key pass to wait for the slide (EditModeArrival.nextWaitsForTheSlide). Profiled 2026-09-30 with xctrace Time Profiler against the probe, samples cut to the 500ms after each Cmd-2: about 480ms busy per switch either way; about 270ms of it is per-frame NSHostingView.layout while canvas/panel/dock frames animate. Into Edit, SwiftUI AccessibilityNode.updateFocusResponder was about 28ms per switch (walks the whole responder tree after every render, grows with every view built), AccessibilityViewGraph.update about 10ms more. Per frame the canvas updateNSView runs CanvasNSView.apply → refreshOverlaysInsideTransaction, refreshLayerSelectionDisplay, canvasNameLabels because canvasViewSizeChanged writes a new viewport each frame. Stage costs: key pass ~50ms, timeline+tool bar ~80, track rows ~90 (captions lane with 191 cues and words lane), panel sections 15 to 45ms each (CaptionStylePreview, PanelFieldRowLayout, SystemSegments.sizeThatFits). Measure with a filmWindow step (docs/design/playtest-harness.md) rather than mainBusy alone.
acceptance: On the five minute captioned sample, the tool bar and track rows are drawn within 350ms of Command 2, and the panel's sections follow just after the slide, never part way through it

view-to-edit-on-a-long-recording-walk passes three runs in a row: the filmed slide never sits still for 30ms in its first 330ms, and no main-thread pass reaches 100 ms (it failed at 118.6 ms in the 2026-10-20 sweep and about 135 ms on 2026-10-06)
The main thread is busy for well under half of the 0.8s after Command 2 (about 630 to 680ms on 2026-09-30)

log.note: Reproduced 2026-10-02 (screen locked, forced walk): View to Edit on the 5 min captioned sample, slide lands ~280ms, ruler ~360ms, tool bar and rows ~400-435ms, panel sections until ~800ms; main thread 615ms of 0.8s. xctrace: almost all of it is SwiftUI/AppKit layout and commit, app code tiny.

Adversarial review: no build cost can fit in the 60ms between the slide landing (~290ms) and 350ms, and building during the slide stutters it (2026-09-30), so the pieces have to exist before Cmd-2. Built Edit's pieces behind View, out of sight, after 0.6s idle, paused while playing, kept for the window's life. Risks checked: View playback cost (hidden tracks sleep while hidden: +8% main thread, was +25%), walks finding hidden controls (out of reach once the slide lands), accessibility (hidden after the slide), Cmd-1 latency (same as baseline, 46-88ms first picture).

Finding: a full panel sliding in halves the slide's pictures (16-18 in 330ms, 26-40ms stills) however it moves: offset, width, mask, fixed height, own hosting view, under the canvas, compositingGroup, geometryGroup, opacity 0, no dropdowns, still reels all measured, none helped; only fewer mounted sections did (Captions section is the heavy one). So the panel is behind View only with next-panel-with-the-slide (off); by default it fills a section a pass after the slide (Time ~0.30s, Captions ~0.38s).

Acceptance: (1) tool bar and track rows drawn within the slide (~0.3s) MET; panel sections by ~0.38s NOT MET by default (met with the switch, at the cost of (2)). (2) filmed slide longest still 18-20ms in 4 runs MET (walk claims it; baseline measured 37-45ms the same day). (3) main thread 550-600ms of 0.8s NOT MET (baseline 533-639): it is the window drawing the slide at full rate, the slide back to View costs the same; not reachable without making SwiftUI frames cheaper. Suite 10911 green; 17 related walks green (13 forced under a lock; an-editing-session and video-tool-bar fail identically on the old code under a lock). Commit 4bce21d4. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-02-edit-arrives-with-the-slide.json.

triage 2026-11-13: epic video-editing -> video-perf. A freeze of over 100 ms switching a long recording to Edit is exactly what the video-perf focus promises away (editing stays instant at any length), so it moves to the head of p2 with the other focus work. The speed walk tools (Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh, rank-trace.py) measure the main thread the same way; the first long-edit fixes (c771adfbb) may already have shrunk it, so measure before fixing.

Measured first on HEAD acaad755 (2026-11-17): the walk ran 3 times; no main-thread pass reached 100ms (longest 46, 66, 89ms), but the filmed slide's longest still was 34, 19 (a false pass, see below) and 31ms against 30. A six-switch film walk: 32-43ms stills on every switch, at two places: 90-130ms after the key (the first slide frames, a 29ms key pass then 28 and 16ms passes) and 300-320ms (the panel's first section and the pieces coming back within reach, both timed at exactly 0.25s, landing on the slide's last frames). Into-Edit main thread busy 700-800ms of 0.8s.

Landed 78370cea2: what waited for the slide (the panel's first section, the pieces coming back within reach) now waits for ViewEditMode.landedSeconds (0.33s) instead of 0.25s, when the slide's last frames were still being drawn. Six filmed switches on one machine state: old code stalled at the slide's end in 2 of 6 (33, 51ms), new in 1 of 6 (34ms). Harness: a failed filmWindow is FailedAfterActing (its retry pressed Cmd-2 in Edit, filmed nothing and passed: that was the 19ms 'pass' this morning), and while the camera rolls the key step no longer describes the editor or rewrites the 500KB log (4-9ms in the slide's first frames).

Where it stands (2026-11-17, after 78370cea2, 3 walk runs): (2) still fails, longest still 39-41ms, all at 90-130ms after the key; no main-thread pass near 100ms (max 58ms in those runs, 89ms in 12 runs today). (1) tool bar and rows come with the slide; panel sections now start ~0.33s. (3) into Edit the main thread is busy 600-720ms of 0.8s. Start stall anatomy (xctrace all processes): key pass ~29ms, then 28 and 16ms frames before the steady 9-10ms ones; extra over a steady frame is SwiftUI accessibility property application, the focus responder walk and NSWindow drag-region recompute, app code under 5%. Tried and dropped: keeping Edit's pieces awake behind View (no change, 32-40ms). Next step for whoever takes this: the slide re-lays out the whole window every frame (main thread full for 270ms), so both bars need the slide to move as layers (end-state layout once, motion by Core Animation) rather than a SwiftUI frame animation; film it against today's. The stills are scattered single missed frames (34ms = two 60Hz frames), at the start (the pass after the key, ~17-20ms) and mid-slide, not one fixed stall.

Per-frame cost (xctrace + os_signpost passes, 6 switches): every slide frame is a full SwiftUI render on the main thread, median 13.5-14.3ms against a 16.7ms frame, back to back with no idle. Split: AttributeGraph ~31%, NSHostingView layout ~28%, accessibility/focus ~19% (incl. the window's drag regions _resetDragMargins/UpdateStructuralRegions ~15-17%), CA commit ~12%. App code ~0. Pass 2 after the key is ~20ms, half of it SwiftUI accessibility (applyProperties, updateFocusResponder walk). With the canvas's PictureMove effect switched off the frame median fell to 11.4ms, so the picture move is 2-3ms a frame.

Tried and dropped (no measurable gain, reverted): (a) the empty panel shell kept mounted behind View with its sections held, so the key inserts nothing: walk film 36, 37, 34ms; (b) the sliding window accessibilityHidden for the slide's 0.35s: walk film 42, 30, 32, 19; (a)+(b): walk 26, 28, 32, 35, 50, 25, 26 but the 8-switch film walk median 34.5 vs HEAD 35 over 24 switches each, and (b) moves the accessibility churn into passes 2-3 and costs VoiceOver its place for the slide. No main-thread pass reached 100ms in any run (max ~70ms, at the panel filling after the landing, same as HEAD).

Next step for whoever takes this: the 30ms bar needs each slide frame well under 16.7ms on a busy machine, and SwiftUI keyframes put a ~14ms main-thread render in every frame. Moving only the canvas into Core Animation (CanvasNSView animating its own layer's transform with a spring matching .smooth(0.25), model value home) saves 2-3ms a frame; the panel and dock would still be SwiftUI-driven, so the whole win needs them in layers SwiftUI does not re-render per frame. Compare builds with the film walk, 3 runs each (24 switches), never one walk's single film. Bar (3), main thread under half of 0.8s, cannot be met while the frames are SwiftUI renders (slide ~260ms busy) and the panel fills in the same 0.8s (~300ms).
